all_found.desc: [BUG] merge=union resurrects a blocker line one branch removed when the other branch's hunk is adjacent: the union emits both sides without a conflict marker, and a later render carries the resurrected line because its ID is unknown to a fresh ledger. Verified in scratch clones: base lists a-009, branch A removes it (fixed), branch B appends c-001 after it; the merge succeeds with a-009 back in FINDINGS.md, where a plain merge would have shown the human the deletion.

rejected.desc: [ADVISORY] The doc says merge=union means never a conflict marker, but GitHub's server-side mergeability check and web merge buttons are not documented to honor .gitattributes merge drivers. A PR may still show 'This branch has conflicts' in the GitHub UI; the doc overclaims.

[ADVISORY] The union attribute also applies to hand-maintained sections the renderer preserves verbatim; two branches editing the same preserved line keep both versions, which never normalize. Duplicated hand-maintained content where a conflict would have warned a human.

[ADVISORY] A union merge lets a hand-edited forged '[granted]' line merge silently without the review a conflict forces. Display only (gates read the ledger); can mislead readers until the next render.
[ADVISORY] The test uses git init -b and git switch -c without skipping on an old or missing git. Hard failure instead of a skip on an old git.

fix@0.summary: The union residue (a line one side removed kept beside the other side addition) is documented as the deliberate fail-safe trade and pinned: FINDINGS.md is display only, and a render from a ledger that knows the finding retires the resurrected line. Docs note GitHub web merge may not honor merge drivers.
